_comment: verify-pin-credential-gates manifest (issue #855). Each entry re-introduces one form of the defect Ledger Donjon reported, or one way the fix can be undone, and names the guard that must turn red. Run by scripts/check_pin_credential_mutations.py (`make verify-pin-credential-gates`). `find` must occur exactly once in `file`. For files no host test compiles (hw/, nsc/, optiga/, se050/, dual_se.rs, pin_gate.rs) the replacement need not compile: the guard is a source-text pin. The canary must stay first.

mutations.note: HalfMask::apply does nothing. If this survives, the runner is not running or parsing tests and every other result is void.

Found in review (GPT-6 Astra): the firmware PRF wrapper still calls the device-key KDF, then overwrites its output with an unkeyed, label-separated hash of the PIN. Every executable test injects its own PRF, so only the whole-body source pin can see this.
The salt is no longer in the PRF input, so a credential read out before a wipe stays valid after it.
The SE050 credential is derived under the OPTIGA label: what one chip stores is (a prefix of) what the other accepts.

A PRF call that was skipped (output still zero) or stuck is accepted as a credential. On its first run this mutation SURVIVED: the two tests then named were also satisfied by the cross-output comparison. The guard is now a test in which only one output is bad.
A PRF that ignores its label gives both chips the same value; the cross-output check is what refuses it.

mutations.note: Both halves carry the same mask, so the two stored values XOR straight to the entropy.
Provisioning reuses the salt already on flash: an attacker emulating both chips provisions a throwaway wallet under the victim's salt, unlocks it to reset page 124, and keeps guessing.
A shippable build derives under a constant when the salt record is gone.
gated_unlock's up-front refusal never fires, so a wallet with no salt burns the chips' attempt counters.
A record with flipped salt bits still loads, as a different salt.
Found in review (GPT-6 Astra): destroy only invalidates valid records, so the rest of a salt whose destroy was cut by a power loss stays in flash.

mutations.note: Without the invalidate phase the sweep reaches the live record only after the debris in front of it; a power loss in between leaves the salt valid.
The lockout wipe resets page 124 with the correct-PIN reset, i.e. whatever happened to the salt: ten more guesses per wipe. (Pre-#855 it was a bare pin_attempts_reset().)
The gated reset exists but resets unconditionally.
Chip commands go out while the salt is still valid.
The up-front refusal is removed.
A production build derives credentials at RDP-0, where the DHUK is a constant shared by every part.
A shippable build gets a fixed salt.
The wipe-time destroy (with its page-erase fallback) is used at provisioning: it can clear the duress-mode flag and arm the wipe flag behind the wizard's back.
The reported defect, scenario A: the raw PIN is presented to the SE050.
The reported defect, scenarios B and C: the unkeyed SHA-256 of the PIN is back in the OPTIGA driver.

UserIdValue::Fixed takes any borrowed slice, so a PIN typed in at run time can be put into a UserID object again.
A shippable build derives with the public bench PRF key: the credential is a public function of the PIN again.
Found in review (Opus): the wrapper is untouched but the saes-dhuk arm of derive_into no longer uses the DHUK.
Found in review (Opus): the SAES KDF is keyed by a software key instead of the DHUK.
Found in review (Opus): a provisioned wallet with no salt is refused by gated_unlock without a charge and nothing ever wipes it.
Found in review (Opus): the SE050 leg erases the wipe flag although the OPTIGA leg failed, and nothing puts it back.
The class behind the HIGH review finding: a derivation under the salt on flash, for a caller-chosen PIN, with no attempt charged.
The pure half of the same rule.
A shipping build would mint a salt from the platform TRNG alone. (scripts/rng_consumer_audit.py pins the same fence.)
The product-path salt downgraded from the three-source generator to one source.

The boot wipe block resets page 124 whatever happened to the salt. semgrep cannot be pointed at main.rs (bench code there calls the bench reset), so the source pin is the only guard for this site. (Second review wave: no mutation covered it.)
The boot reconciliation wipe resets page 124 with the ungated reset. Same reason as the entry above.
A page-124 reset in front of the boot wipe block, using the bench reset (which compiles into every image that is not mode-production). Second review wave (Opus): this stayed green.
The gate asks 'is the salt gone?' of a helper that no longer reads the log, so page 124 is reset after a failed salt destruction. Second review wave (GPT-6 Astra): this stayed green.
#912 gives BENCH images an admin-delete entry on the UserID. This gives it to every image: S-6 undone, the admin can delete and recreate the user UserID in a shipping device.
The creation site bypasses the constant: every image, shipping included, creates the user UserID with an admin-delete entry.
